message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision for this Monopoly turn.

I have six properties and $387 cash. Player 1 has a full orange monopoly and owns several utilities.

Player 1 holds two of three orange properties. Player 3 owns three railroads and one pink property. Player 4 controls New York Avenue and Boardwalk. Several utilities are unowned.

This is my post-turn action. I cannot build. I will keep B&O and Ventnor to block other players' monopolies.

I cannot trade for the unowned Pennsylvania Avenue or Oriental. I will keep Connecticut Avenue as a backup light blue property.

No trade can complete a color set for me. The missing pieces are mostly bank-owned. Player 4 refused to sell New York Avenue to player 1. Player 3 needs my B&O for his fourth railroad.

Player 4 has cash and wants a color set. Player 1 will not sell oranges for cash. I am considering offering something to player 4.

Player 4 cannot complete a color set with me. I could trade for Marvin Gardens to block player 1's yellow monopoly, but that would cost me a valuable property.

I rejected trading Ventnor to player 1 because it would give them two of three yellows and leave the Atlantic unowned. A Connecticut-for-Vermont swap is pointless. Mortgaging is unnecessary since I have enough cash. I am still looking for a clever trade.

Player 3's offers are unappealing. Illinois and St Charles are single-color properties that cannot complete a set. A railroad swap would not be worthwhile because player 3 would still retain two railroads. Mediterranean Avenue is nearly worthless since Baltic is unowned.

Player 1 is the biggest threat if they complete their orange monopoly. Player 4 has cash but few properties. Player 3's railroad income is partially blocked by me.

I will end the turn without trading or mortgaging. Landing on Pennsylvania Avenue would give me a green monopoly, but building houses there costs too much with only $387 cash.

Green houses pay well, but I would need to mortgage other properties to fund them. Light blue houses offer the best return per dollar spent. I should land on unowned properties such as Pennsylvania Avenue, Oriental, Baltic, or Atlantic.

I will not propose trades that reveal my strategy or annoy other players. Purchasing Boardwalk from player 4 would be too expensive and would not complete a color set. I am now considering offering player 1 something in exchange for Marvin Gardens or Vermont, preparing for when bank-owned properties become available.

I realized that owning two of three yellows would give me leverage when Atlantic becomes unowned. Player 1 rejected cash offers for oranges, so I cannot buy Marvin Gardens from them.

Marvin Gardens is worth little on its own. Player 1 might sell it for a premium if they cannot complete the yellow set without Ventnor. I cannot afford a $400 offer with only $387 cash, so I am considering offering Connecticut Avenue plus cash instead.

I will end the turn without trading. I am keeping my current position and will not reveal strategy in a public message.
